simpledes: Net personal wealth is  the total value of non-financial and financial assets (housing, land, deposits, bonds, equities, etc.) held by households, minus their debts. technicaldes: [Net personal wealth]=[Personal non-financial assets]+[Personal financial assets]-[Personal debt]
longtype: Income or wealth shares. longpop: The base unit is the individual (rather than the household) but resources are split equally within couples.
longage: The population is comprised of individuals over age 20.

The survey distributions are fitted using generalized Pareto interpolation. Consumption distributions, where applicable, are converted to income using income-to-consumption ratios. Top incomes are corrected using the fiscal-to-survey profile estimated from Lebanese tax data. Years without observations are interpolated between observed years or extrapolated from the nearest observed year. See data_quality.

method: Distributional national accounts for Australia. Pretax national income is distributed among equal-split adults aged 20 and over, from ALife taxation microdata and the Survey of Income and Housing, adjusted to Australian national accounts aggregates. Source microdata is restricted access. 1991-2018 follows the published series. From 2019 the top percentile is built from Australian Taxation Office published tabulations rather than taxation microdata, which may introduce a break within the top percentile. Estimates from 2020 are rescaled by a smoothed bracket-specific factor calibrated on the overlap with the earlier series, so that the change of source does not itself shift the level. Estimates for 2024 extend the pipeline using the 2023-24 Australian Taxation Office tabulations for the top percentile and the 2024 Australian System of National Accounts for each income component's total, holding the within-component distribution at 2023. Estimates for 2025 are extrapolated from 2024. Before 1912, pretax income shares estimated based on methodology in long-run paper (see sources).

method: Distributional national accounts for Canada. Pretax national income is distributed among equal-split adults aged 20 and over, from Longitudinal Administrative Databank tabulations supplied by Statistics Canada under restricted access. 1982-2023 follows the Canada DINA series, which documents the method through 2021. Detail above the top percentile is obtained by generalized Pareto interpolation within the brackets reported by that series. 2020-2022 are revised relative to the previous update, following revisions to the Canadian national accounts. In years where the source series reports a higher average in the first percentile than the second, reflecting offsetting losses, the first percentile is lowered and the difference redistributed in proportion across percentiles 2 to 50; group aggregates are unaffected. 2024-2025 are extrapolated from 2023. Values at benchmark years are aligned with World Inequality Lab Technical Note 2025/10. Before 1920, pretax income shares estimated based on methodology in long-run paper (see sources).

From 1951 onwards, we have NSSO surveys which we combine with tax tabulations to estimate the distribution of incomes. We extract a full distribution of top incomes from tax tabulations using generalized Pareto interpolation. For bottom incomes, we begin by estimating a consumption distribution to which we apply percentile-level scaling factors (derived from the IHDS survey) to arrive at bottom incomes. We assume surveys are representative till the 90th percentile (p1). We assume tax tabulations are representative from some percentile p2 (> p90) determined by the number of tax filers. Between p1 and p2, we interpolate incomes using a convex junction profile. Overall, ur full distribution series spans 1951-2022, while our estimates for the top 1% share go back till 1922. Before 1980, series is constructed based on the trend observed in the fiscal income data available (see sources). Before 1922, pretax income shares estimated based on methodology in long-run paper (see sources).

The survey distributions are fitted using generalized Pareto interpolation. Consumption distributions, where applicable, are converted to income using income-to-consumption ratios. Top incomes are corrected using the fiscal-to-survey profile estimated from Lebanese tax data. Years without observations are interpolated between observed years or extrapolated from the nearest observed year. See data_quality.

method: Distributional national accounts for New Zealand. Pretax national income is distributed among equal-split adults aged 20 and over. 2001-2021 is constructed from administrative tax microdata in the Integrated Data Infrastructure maintained by Stats NZ, combined with the Household Economic Survey, and adjusted to national accounts aggregates. 2022-2024 are modeled from Inland Revenue tabulations. Detail above the top percentile is obtained by generalized Pareto interpolation. 1920-2000 retains the previously published series, rescaled to join the 2001 estimate; where that rescaling leaves a bracket average out of order the bracket is linearly interpolated from its neighbors and the year renormalized, which affects roughly fifteen brackets a year before 2001 and none from 2001 onward. 2025 is extrapolated from 2024. Top shares in 2021 reflect income timing ahead of the 39 per cent top marginal rate effective April 2021. The method follows Forward (2026); the series were supplied by the author in October 2026 and incorporate revisions subsequent to that work, including a revised treatment of imputation credits on dividend income earned through trusts. Before 1921, pretax income shares estimated based on methodology in long-run paper (see sources).
